page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-64xCPU-512GB is a memory-optimized virtual server belonging to the Cloud Native family. It is powered by an AMD EPYC 7542 processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture, offering 64 vCPUs and 64 physical cores with a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The CPU allocation is shared, and the hypervisor is KVM. It features 512.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 8.0 GB of RAM per core. This server does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, but it comes with one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark results indicate a clear contrast between single-core and multi-core capabilities. The single-core CPU performance in stress-ng is in the bottom 10%, and LLM text generation with a medium 7B model is also in the bottom 10%. However, multi-core performance is robust, with passmark CPU scores, extended instructions, encryption, and physics tests all ranking in the top 25%. Memory performance is solid, featuring top 25% cached read-only memory bandwidth and average uncached read/write speeds. Redis SET operations also perform strongly, reaching the top 25% tier.

The shared CPU allocation presents a tradeoff, as single-threaded tasks are relatively slow, but the massive 512.0 GB memory capacity and strong multi-core scaling provide high resource density. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, this server offers a high volume of memory and cores without the premium of dedicated CPU pinning or bundled local NVMe storage. It is best suited for memory-intensive workloads that scale across multiple threads, such as large-scale database operations, caching layers like Redis, multi-threaded decompression tasks, and general-purpose memory-heavy application hosting.
